nonvacuity: scratch/Nonvacuity.lean compiled independently of Challenge: both positive two-cell laws, interior true propensities, the attained logistic probabilities, printed-odds weighted share 27/28 != 1/4, and recovery of both original cells by reciprocal odds. There are no external hypotheses; the likelihood encodes the specified eight observations. See claim-checks.md for the full printed-reading checklist.

scratch/Nonvacuity.lean constructs all hypotheses with Omega=Fin 2, counting measure, pi=1/2, fR=(1/4,3/4), fO=(3/4,1/4), and computes Z=7/3. scratch/InfiniteMass.lean independently constructs positive unit-integral integrable densities on counting measure over Nat: fR(n)=(1/2)(1/2)^n and fO(n)=(3/4)(1/4)^n. Their square ratio is constantly 1/3, hence Z=infinity. Both files compile without Challenge imports.

The specified witness is a standard normal outcome shared by both potential arms, an independent common Bernoulli(4/5) passing indicator, and an independent fair assignment. scratch/NormalWitness.lean independently compiles probability normalization, always-passer mass 4/5, the exact standard-normal observed law, atomlessness, and finite first absolute moment. All remaining witness conditions, including per-arm independence, positive arm/passing masses, ratio 1/4, full support, and the strictly negative lower-tail mean contradicting the zero target mean, are checked mathematically in claim-checks.md. The check does not invoke any audited Challenge theorem.

scratch/OneArm.lean independently compiles an explicit probability measure on Population 1 0, the pushforward of a standard normal outcome with the sole arm assigned and passing always. It constructs every hypothesis: positive always-passer mass, atomless conditional potential-passer law, and integrability on the potential-passing event. The universal fixed-mass assertion applies, in particular, at discarded share p=1/4. Quantile p=0 is also meaningful and selects the entire law. No Challenge theorem is used.

scratch/OneArm.lean independently constructs every hypothesis for the same explicit nonconstant Gaussian population: probability, per-arm independence of the constant assignment, positive arm mass and observed passing rate, positive always-passer mass, atomless observed response, and integrability on the observed passer-arm event. Its trimming ratio is zero, so the finite-branch implication is active. claim-checks.md additionally checks the nonzero-ratio two-arm normal common-check witness mathematically.
